strategy: heat (used by 70% of respondents; mean pain relief 6.5/10; adverse events 15.9%, burns including blistering)
partner_action: Bring a heat pack or patch that holds a controlled temperature, and check in on the skin underneath. Burns are the most reported downside.

strategy: rest (used by 68% of respondents; mean pain relief 5.3/10; adverse events 7.3%, increased fatigue, increased depression)
partner_action: Take tasks off her plate and protect the space to lie down without her having to ask or justify it.
source_repo: Armour et al. 2019, BMC Complement Altern Med 19:17, doi:10.1186/s12906-019-2431-x

strategy: meditation or breathing (used by 47% of respondents; mean pain relief 4.6/10; adverse events 3.4%, none above threshold)
partner_action: Offer to do a breathing exercise together, and keep the room quiet. Lowest downside of anything in the survey.
source_repo: Armour et al. 2019, BMC Complement Altern Med 19:17, doi:10.1186/s12906-019-2431-x

strategy: massage (used by 32% of respondents; mean pain relief 5.5/10; adverse events 6.8%, none above threshold)
partner_action: Offer a back or shoulder massage, and follow her direction on pressure and location.
source_repo: Armour et al. 2019, BMC Complement Altern Med 19:17, doi:10.1186/s12906-019-2431-x

strategy: acupressure (used by 8% of respondents; mean pain relief 6.3/10; adverse events 7.1%, none above threshold)
partner_action: Ask whether pressure on a specific point helps, and hold it for her.
source_repo: Armour et al. 2019, BMC Complement Altern Med 19:17, doi:10.1186/s12906-019-2431-x

strategy: cold (used by 5% of respondents; mean pain relief 5.5/10; adverse events 5.6%, none above threshold)
partner_action: Have a cold pack ready as an alternative when heat is not helping.

strategy: stretching (used by 40% of respondents; mean pain relief 4.6/10; adverse events 14.8%, increased pelvic pain, increased nausea, increased flare ups)
partner_action: Suggest gentle stretching only, and stop at the first sign it is making things worse.
source_repo: Armour et al. 2019, BMC Complement Altern Med 19:17, doi:10.1186/s12906-019-2431-x

strategy: yoga or Pilates (used by 35% of respondents; mean pain relief 4.5/10; adverse events 15.9%, increased pelvic pain)
partner_action: Good on steady days. The reported pain increases were linked mostly to Pilates rather than yoga, so favour yoga.
source_repo: Armour et al. 2019, BMC Complement Altern Med 19:17, doi:10.1186/s12906-019-2431-x

strategy: taichi or qigong (used by 2% of respondents; mean pain relief 4.0/10; adverse events 0.0%, none reported)
partner_action: Offer as a low intensity movement option. No adverse events were reported, though very few people used it.
source_repo: Armour et al. 2019, BMC Complement Altern Med 19:17, doi:10.1186/s12906-019-2431-x

strategy: exercise (used by 42% of respondents; mean pain relief 4.9/10; adverse events 34.2%, increased pelvic pain, increased fatigue, increased flare ups)
partner_action: Do NOT push exercise during a flare up. One in three users reported it made things worse. Offer it only on steady days, and let her set the pace.
